steps.text: Set your preferences, select automatic or manual execution, and run the practice account first.

pros: No platform fees on top of spreads.
Risk settings before the first trade.
A browser dashboard - nothing to install.
cons: Asset list that shifts between pages.
The headline fee claim and the real cost disagree.
Two conflicting support figures.
Restriction lists disagree.
redFlags: Ownership details missing from the public pages.
The demo promised in the pitch but buried in the flow.
A score and a community mood wearing the same number.

faqs.a: 9 crypto assets through broker partners, per the published pages. The list varies between sections, so check the dashboard after signup.
The platform fee is absent, but every trade carries a broker spread the page itself calls the real cost. The headline says free; the fine print says otherwise. Budget for the fine print.

faqs.q: What happens after I sign up?
faqs.a: You confirm the account by email, fund US$250, set your risk preferences and choose automatic or manual mode. The demo account runs alongside while you learn.
Yes - the platform offers automatic and manual modes, so you can follow the signals or confirm each entry yourself.

faqs.q: Does it offer a demo account?
faqs.a: Yes - a practice account is part of the package and runs alongside the live balance, which is the sensible first step before risking the US$250 minimum.

bottomLine: The service behind the marketing looks functional, and a careful user can use it without stepping on the fine print.
Our 4.4 reflects what the pages publish and what they skip. It is not a warning off - it is a reminder to trade the product, not the pitch.
